meaning: Archives TASK-20260913-c43d3e's consolidation of EXP-CRYPTO-5e8beb into implementation-v3/, closing the two REVISE-blocking findings from the independent implementation review TASK-20260908-0eabfe (C8: no panel-advantage scoring logic existed anywhere in the codebase; C10: the guarded launch-admission check performed existence-only verification on all four required bindings instead of genuine content checks) plus the minor C9 finding (TRAP_HORIZON/REFERENCE_TRAP_HORIZON were declared but never actually referenced by the trap-distribution functions, which hardcoded exactly two steps) and this task's own additional requirement to replace runtime_preflight.py's unconditional always-refuses stub with real, side-effect-free host capability probing. Before this archive, the Coordinator independently re-verified every material claim rather than trusting the executor's self-report: fixtures.py, kernels.py, certificates.py were confirmed byte-identical (via sha256) to their originals in experiments/EXP-CRYPTO-5e8beb/implementation/, and panel_scoring.py byte-identical to implementation-v2/'s already-validated version (TASK-20260908-630c49's scorer_and_nonadmission_fidelity joint). The C9 fix was independently re-executed (not merely re-read): both the old hardcoded and new TRAP_HORIZON-driven trap_real_distribution/trap_comparison_distribution (transcripts.py) and reference_trap_real_distribution/reference_trap_comparison_distribution (reference.py) were run side-by-side across all 11 assumption-trap starts, with zero mismatches, confirming the generalization is behavior-preserving at the frozen TRAP_HORIZON=2. The C10 admission logic was exercised with an independently-authored (not copied from the executor's own tests) valid launch-binding bundle plus four independently-authored broken variants -- a tampered implementation file whose sha256 no longer matches the manifest, an expired launch lock, a launch lock with a sibling release file, and a review receipt with a failing verdict -- and in every case the correct outcome (pass or a specifically-named refusal) was observed. The new runtime_preflight.py probes were executed directly against this container and their live output (cgroup v2 controller file present but unreadable; Docker binary found but daemon unreachable, exit code 1; RLIMIT_AS/RLIMIT_CPU successfully read back as unlimited) matches exactly what implementation-report.yaml discloses. All 8 implementation_files_sha256 entries in implementation-v3's own implementation-manifest.yaml were independently recomputed and matched with zero discrepancies. python3 -m py_compile is clean on all 8 .py files, and a full grep sweep confirmed the only call sites of fixtures.iter_partition_specs() with the real frozen parameters are (a) inside certificates.py's pre-existing, byte-identical-to-original expected-path/expected-count helpers, which only read static (index, N) metadata and never generate an actual permutation, and (b) driver.main()'s post-admission branch, which this task never reaches (no genuine launch lock exists for TASK-20260913-c43d3e; check_launch_admission's own fail-closed logic, itself independently verified above, is what prevents it, not merely a promise not to call it). No experiments/EXP-CRYPTO-5e8beb/runs/ directory exists, and implementation/ and implementation-v2/ are confirmed untouched by git status. scientific_execution_authorized remains false throughout; implementation-report.yaml records scientific_runs=0 and fixtures_evaluated_on_frozen_panel=0. This archive authorizes no scientific launch. A future scientific-execution task still requires: a fresh independent implementation review of this exact implementation-v3 content (no review has examined it, since it differs materially from every prior review's target), a genuine launch lock naming this exact write scope, and real (not this task's necessarily-nondestructive read-only) cgroup/Docker admission on the actual target host.
